must_preserve: The specific geometric skeleton of the letter 'K' (vertical bar on left, two diagonal strokes on right)
The distinct gap/separation between the upper-right diagonal stroke and the central vertex
The presence and relative position (top-right) of the four-pointed star symbol
The rounded terminals (caps) of the 'K' strokes
can_restyle: Background color gradient (can shift hue but should remain dark/mysterious)
Material of the 'K' (can be metallic, neon, glass, etc., instead of flat white)
Style of the star (can be glowing, outlined, or integrated into the theme)
must_not_replace_with: Generic letters without the specific Keep 'K' cut
color_preservation: The brand identity relies heavily on the contrast between the bright foreground element and the deep purple background. While the exact hex code can adapt to a theme, the 'Purple + Bright Accent' relationship is crucial. Do not change the background to plain white or black unless the theme strictly demands high contrast monochrome.
structure_summary: A minimalist, lowercase-style 'k' constructed from thick, rounded strokes. The defining feature is the floating upper-right leg that does not touch the central junction. A small four-pointed star floats in the upper right quadrant, acting as a secondary brand mark.
risk_notes: Do not connect the upper-right stroke to the rest of the 'K', as this destroys the specific Keep logo recognition.
Do not remove the star; it distinguishes this specific version of the logo from a generic letter K.
Avoid making the 'K' too thin; it requires visual weight to be readable at small sizes.
